units.translation: The charm of beautiful statues is hateful to a man, and in the absence of eyes all Aphrodite is gone.
the land of Aphrodite rich in wheat.
May Ares, the mortal-destroying bedfellow of Aphrodite, not shear off the flower.
The fate of Aphrodite has been given to Harmonia.

foam of human food flowed down from the mouth.

heaps of corpses — voiceless they will signal to the eyes of mortals.

Correctly written Αχαικῶν [of the Achaeans] and Αχαικού [of the Achaean], not Αχαϊκ— [Achaean], as is sometimes written in the books of Euripides, which is a later form. On both forms see Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 2732,
